items.q: Which is the ITIL definition of a service?
o: A configuration of an organization's resources designed to offer value for a consumer
A means of enabling value co-creation by facilitating outcomes that customers want to achieve, without the customer having to manage specific costs and risks
A formal description of one or more products designed for a target consumer group
A series of steps an organization undertakes to deliver value to consumers
items.x: A service enables value co-creation by facilitating outcomes customers want, without them having to manage specific costs and risks. Option A defines a product, and option D describes a value stream.

items.q: The head of logistics defines the requirements for a new route-planning service and is accountable for the results the business gets from using it. Which role is this person performing?
items.x: The customer defines the requirements for products and services and takes responsibility for the outcomes of service consumption. The sponsor authorizes the budget and the user uses the service.

items.q:
Identify the missing word in the following sentence.
A [?] is a person who uses services.
items.x: A user is a person who uses services. One person can hold several roles, for example a home user who chooses (customer), pays for (sponsor) and uses (user) a mobile plan.

items.q: What is a service offering?
o: A cooperation between a service provider and a service consumer
A configuration of resources designed to offer value
A formal description of one or more services, designed to address the needs of a target consumer group
A documented agreement about the expected level of service
items.x: A service offering formally describes one or more services for a target consumer group and may include goods, access to resources and service actions. Option A is a service relationship and option D an SLA.

items.q: A design agency subscribes to a service that gives it 2 TB of cloud storage. Ownership of the storage stays with the provider. Which component of the service offering is this?
items.x: Access to resources grants the consumer the use of the provider's resources under agreed terms without transferring ownership. Goods transfer ownership, and service actions are activities performed for the consumer.

items.q: Which of the following is an example of service PROVISION?
o: Fulfilling an agreed service action for a user
A user requesting a service action
A consumer training its staff to use a new service
A consumer receiving goods from a provider
items.x: Service provision covers the activities a provider performs to provide services, such as managing its resources, fulfilling agreed service actions and improving service performance. Options B to D are service consumption activities.

items.q: What is an output?
o: A result for a stakeholder enabled by one or more outcomes
The perceived benefits of a service
The functionality offered by a product
A tangible or intangible deliverable of an activity
items.x: An output is a tangible or intangible deliverable of an activity, such as a report or a deployed feature. An outcome is a result for a stakeholder enabled by one or more outputs.

items.q: A retailer moves its online shop to a cloud platform. Which of the following is a risk IMPOSED on the retailer by using the service?
o: Failure of the retailer's own ageing servers
A security breach at the cloud provider affecting the retailer's data
Outdated hardware in the retailer's data centre
items.x: A security breach at the provider is a risk introduced by consuming the service. The other options are risks that the service removes from the retailer.

items.q: Which of the following describes the WARRANTY of an online banking service?
o: The service will be available 99.95% of the time and data is encrypted
Customers can transfer money between accounts
Customers can set up recurring payments
items.x: Warranty is assurance that a product or service will meet agreed requirements, such as availability, capacity, security and continuity. Transfers, statements and recurring payments are utility: what the service does.

items.q: What is a problem?
o: An unplanned interruption to a service
A cause, or potential cause, of one or more incidents
A request for a change to a service
A known error that has a permanent fix
items.x: A problem is a cause, or potential cause, of one or more incidents. Problem management investigates problems so that the likelihood and impact of incidents are reduced.

items.q: Which is the BEST description of a service request?
o: An unplanned interruption reported by a user
A cause of one or more incidents
A change that must be implemented immediately
A request from a user or a user's authorized representative that initiates a service action that has been agreed as a normal part of service delivery
items.x: Service requests are normal, pre-defined requests such as access requests, information requests or new equipment. Nothing is broken, which is what distinguishes them from incidents.

items.q: What is the main focus of an experience level agreement (XLA)?
o: The legal penalties a supplier pays for failures
The technical uptime of infrastructure components
The experience and outcomes that users and customers actually perceive
The internal targets agreed between two support teams
items.x: XLAs complement traditional SLAs by targeting experience outcomes, such as how productive and satisfied users are, rather than only technical metrics. This helps avoid the 'watermelon effect', where SLA reports are green but users are unhappy.

items.q: The service desk keeps giving users wrong answers because its knowledge base is out of date. Which dimension of product and service management is MOST directly affected?
items.x: The information and technology dimension covers the information and knowledge needed to manage products and services, as well as the technologies that support them. An outdated knowledge base is an information problem.

items.q: An organization has always preferred to keep work in-house and is reluctant to use external suppliers. Which factor influencing supplier strategy does this describe?
items.x: Corporate culture, including a historical preference for in-house or outsourced work, influences supplier strategy. Others include strategic focus, resource scarcity, cost concerns, subject matter expertise, external constraints and demand patterns.

items.q: Which dimension focuses on how the various parts of the organization work in an integrated and coordinated way to enable value creation through products and services?
items.x: The value streams and processes dimension defines the activities, workflows, controls and procedures needed to create value, and how they fit together.

items.q: To which of the following should the four dimensions of product and service management be applied?
o: Only to new products and services
Only to the information technology department
Only to products delivered by external suppliers
To each product and service and to the value system as a whole
items.x: The four dimensions should be considered for every product and service and for the value system as a whole, in a balanced way. Neglecting a dimension can cause products and services to underperform.

items.q: Before committing any resources, a team analyses demand signals and market opportunities and checks how a proposed product fits the organization's strategy. Which lifecycle activity is this?
items.x: Discover identifies needs, demand and opportunities and aligns them with strategy before resources are committed. Design then turns validated needs into specifications, architectures and prototypes.

items.q: Developers create, configure and test a new mobile app feature in a test environment before it is moved into the live environment. Which lifecycle activity is this?
items.x: Build creates, configures and tests the solution. Transition then moves the new or changed product into the live environment.

items.q: A platform team monitors a live product and keeps it running to its agreed performance and reliability targets. Which lifecycle activity is this?
items.x: Operate keeps the live product running to agreed performance and reliability targets. Support helps users and restores normal operation when something goes wrong.

items.q: Which of the following is NOT an activity of the ITIL product and service lifecycle?
items.x: The activities are Discover, Design, Acquire, Build, Transition, Operate, Deliver and Support. Engage was a value chain activity in ITIL 4.

items.q: Which guiding principle warns that measurement must be used carefully, and recommends observing the current state directly where possible?
items.x: 'Start where you are' recommends assessing the current state objectively, including by direct observation, because data can be incomplete and the act of measuring can affect results.

items.q: A product manager spends time with users to understand how they actually use the service, what helps them reach their goals and what frustrates them. Which guiding principle is MOST directly being applied?
items.x: Applying 'focus on value' includes knowing who the consumers are, how they use each product or service, and their experience, so that work stays linked to what they value.

items.q: A team releases a minimum viable version of a self-service portal to a pilot group, collects comments and improves it every two weeks. Which guiding principle is being applied?
items.x: Delivering in small, usable increments and using feedback to adjust is 'progress iteratively with feedback'. Fast does not mean incomplete: each iteration should deliver something useful.

items.q: 'Collaboration does not mean consensus' is guidance for applying which guiding principle?
items.x: Involving the right stakeholders does not mean everyone must agree before acting. Decisions still need to be made by the appropriate people, based on visible information.

items.q: 'Recognize the complexity of the systems' is a recommendation for applying which guiding principle?
items.x: Working holistically requires understanding how complex the system is. Different levels of complexity need different approaches, so look for patterns and collaborate across the system.

items.q: 'Do fewer things, but do them better' is advice for applying which guiding principle?
items.x: 'Keep it simple and practical' recommends concentrating on fewer, valuable activities and doing them well, respecting people's time and favouring practical solutions.

items.q: Which of the following is a recommendation for applying the 'optimize and automate' principle?
o: Define your metrics, so that the effect of optimization and automation can be measured
Automate as many tasks as possible before analysing them
Avoid involving stakeholders, to keep the work fast
Start by buying the most advanced automation tool available
items.x: When applying 'optimize and automate': simplify and optimize before automating, define your metrics, and use the other guiding principles at the same time.

items.q: What is a governing body?
o: A team that approves all changes
An external regulator that audits the organization
A person or group of people accountable at the highest level for the performance and compliance of the organization
items.x: The governing body, for example a board of directors, is accountable at the highest level. It evaluates, directs and monitors the organization.

items.q: In governance, which activity involves assigning responsibility for, and directing the preparation and implementation of, organizational strategy and policies?
items.x: 'Direct' sets direction through strategies and policies. 'Evaluate' reviews the organization and its environment, and 'monitor' checks performance and conformance with policies and direction.

items.q: In which step of the continual improvement model are measurable targets for the improvement defined?
o: Where do we want to be?
How do we keep the momentum going?
items.x: 'Where do we want to be?' defines the target state, typically with measurable targets such as critical success factors and key performance indicators, based on the vision and the gap from the baseline.

items.q: Who is responsible for continual improvement in an organization?
o: Everyone in the organization, although a dedicated team may lead and coordinate it
items.x: Continual improvement is everyone's responsibility at every level. A dedicated team can champion and coordinate it, but it should not be left to one group.

items.q: An improvement project was completed on time and on budget. What should the step 'Did we get there?' check?
o: Whether the project documents were archived
Whether the project team has been released
Whether the next improvement has been approved
Whether the measurable targets and the expected value were actually achieved
items.x: A plan can be executed perfectly and still fail to deliver the intended value. 'Did we get there?' measures results against the targets and the expected value, and loops back if they were missed.

items.q: Into which two groups are the ITIL (Version 5) management practices organized?
o: General management and product and service management
items.x: Version 5 organizes the 34 management practices into two groups: general management practices and product and service management practices. The separate technical management group of ITIL 4 no longer exists.

items.q: What is the purpose of the problem management practice?
o: To reduce the likelihood and impact of incidents by identifying actual and potential causes of incidents, and managing workarounds and known errors
To restore normal service operation as quickly as possible
To maximize the number of successful changes
To capture demand for incident resolution
items.x: Problem management finds and addresses the causes of incidents and manages workarounds and known errors. Restoring service quickly (B) is incident management.

items.q: What does the ITIL value system describe?
o: Only the order in which projects must be delivered
The financial value of an organization's assets
The reporting lines of the IT department
How all the components and activities of an organization work together as a system to enable value creation
items.x: The value system shows how guiding principles, governance, lifecycle and value chain activities, practices and continual improvement work together to turn opportunity and demand into value.

items.q: Which problem is the ITIL value system specifically designed to help organizations overcome?
o: Organizational silos that prevent effective collaboration
items.x: Silos make organizations rigid and slow. The value system encourages flexibility and integration, so that teams work together across boundaries to create value.

items.q: What is the main purpose of value stream mapping?
o: To visualize the flow of work from demand to value, so that waste, delays and bottlenecks can be identified
To produce a list of all software applications
To calculate the depreciation of IT assets
items.x: Value stream mapping, a Lean technique, visualizes how work flows through the steps of a value stream. It makes waiting times, hand-offs and other waste visible so that the flow can be improved.

items.q: When analysing a value stream, which metric measures the total time from a consumer's request until the product or service is delivered?
items.x: Lead time is the total elapsed time from request to delivery, including waiting. Process time, also called touch time, counts only the time when work is actually being done.

items.q: Which statement BEST describes agentic AI?
o: AI that only generates text in response to a single prompt
A dashboard that reports AI usage
AI systems that can plan and take actions towards goals with a degree of autonomy and limited human intervention
Any automation that uses scripts written by people
items.x: Agentic AI goes beyond producing content. AI agents can plan, decide and act, for example by calling tools or running workflow steps, towards a goal. This makes governance and human oversight especially important.

items.q: How can PRINCE2 be used together with ITIL?
o: PRINCE2 replaces the ITIL guiding principles
PRINCE2 is a service desk tool that implements ITIL
PRINCE2 defines the requirements for ITIL certification of organizations
PRINCE2 is a project management method that can support the delivery of projects within an organization that uses ITIL
items.x: PRINCE2 is a structured project management method. It complements ITIL, for example when new or changed products and services are delivered through projects.
